name: level2-playthrough-win
description: Level 2 (Grumpstone Ridge) playthrough: 3 surveys, a freight warehouse, four far-flung living quarters, five blast-plan cycles and five contract acceptances on a funded ($3,000,000) mine that stays solvent and revolt-free throughout. #1431 (rebuilt after #1313 froze the mine at level end): the original $150,000 opening went bankrupt at tick 176 and the file played on over a lost game; the quarters (placed far from every blast pattern so no blast destroys them) keep wellBeing up and the run ends as a real win: `campaign start level:grumpstone_ridge` is locked on a fresh campaign, so the file runs on the new_game world and closes with `campaign complete level:grumpstone_ridge`, which activates level 2 and ends it 'completed' with profit at the $250,000 threshold. Drillers and blasters die in blasts, so each later pattern re-hires and re-equips a crew and rig.

issue #585 (command-mode-only): raised 6 -> 45 (confirmed via direct trace, createGameEngine + runCommand replay) -- with the freight_warehouse now built (see the vehicle-buy-assign step's own note), storedMassKg still traces flat at 0.0 through the original 6 ticks: the debris_hauler auto-claimed by driver #3 has to walk from its own spawn tile to vehicle #2, drive it roughly 20+ tiles out to the nearest on-ground fragment, load, then drive back to the depot -- none of which lands inside 6 ticks. Traced in 2-tick increments: the first fragment (a mixed-material haul, not pure ore) delivers around tick+16, a second around tick+24, after which delivery plateaus (a separate, deeper HaulDispatch limitation -- the hauler's second dispatch stalls; #552's own known gap) at storedMassKg ~2160kg / collectedOre.rustite ~425kg, comfortably past both group deliveries below. 45 was chosen (not the smaller values that also clear that plateau) because this file's pattern-2 charge order (charge hole:*, well below) is timing-sensitive to the exact absolute tick this step lands on -- smaller offsets (16, 24, 40) left one hole still mid-load when blast 2's own fixed-length charge-wait ran out ("Invalid plan: H11/H15: Charge still loading"), a downstream regression direct trace caught and is not this step's own concern to explain further than to say 45 was verified clean through blast 2 and beyond. #953: raised 45 -> 70 -- the climb-limit gate makes the hauler's ordinary route to its nearest on-ground fragment cost more ticks whenever the route crosses a bench-level boundary (ramp-based multi-level pathing instead of a straight walk); direct trace (npx tsx scripts/run-all-scenarios.ts level2-playthrough-win) confirmed 70 clears the original storedMassKg-plateau this step exists to reach (~795kg stored by this point, comfortably above every downstream contract amount). #973: a separate, pre-existing Logistics.ts issue (consumeStoredOre's rubble branch deleted an oversized stored fragment's entire surplus rather than partially consuming it) meant a contract-deliver step later in this file could still be refused depending on which single fragment happened to be first in storage -- unrelated to this step's own tick value, not fixed by raising it further (traced identical at tick 70/100/250). Fixed in #973 via splitStoredFragmentMass, unrelated to this step's own tick value. #674: interaction mode ran its own, unchanged `tick 6` here -- a 39-tick gap that put every later step of the two modes on different absolute ticks and was the whole of this file own command/interaction divergence (first state-dump difference of the run, tickCount 598 vs 559, everything before it byte-identical). steps.description: Issue #586 CI, this PR: CI reported "Step 96 timed out after 60000ms" twice in a row on this exact step, though it never reproduced across 3 clean local reruns in this session's own investigation -- consistent with a genuine CPU-bound cost spike (not a render-frame cost; interaction batch runs suspend drawing) that only shows up under CI's shared/contended runner (10 concurrent Chrome instances across shards), not a single local run with full CPU access. The preceding step just ordered a fresh 30-hole drill_plan (5x6 grid); tick 150 in one call processes all of that dispatch/pathfinding in a single blocking page.evaluate, an outlier compared to the tick 20/tick 30 chunks used everywhere else in this project's scenario files. Split into 3x tick 50 -- same total simulation-tick advance, same end state. Update: the split alone did not help -- CI reported the identical "Step 96 timed out after 60000ms" again on the next push, because the step-level timeout (DEFAULT_STEP_TIMEOUT, puppeteer-utils.ts) wraps the WHOLE step's cumulative action time, not each action individually (run-all-scenarios.ts/scenario-interaction-runner.ts both compute stepTimeout once per step and race it against the step's full for-loop of actions). The real fix is this step's own  field (ScenarioStepDef.timeout, seconds, scenario-types.ts) -- raised to 120s, comfortably covering CI's slower/contended runner for this step's genuinely CPU-heavy 150-tick advance right after a fresh 30-hole drill_plan. Kept the 3x tick 50 split too (harmless, and slightly more granular progress if a future step ever needs to interrupt mid-way).

CI reported "Step 98 timed out after 60000ms" — the same CPU-bound cost spike as step 96 (see that step's note): this step drains the rest of the same 30-hole drill_plan dispatch/pathfinding backlog from step 95, right after step 96 already paid the first half of that cost. Same fix: raise this step's own timeout to 120s.
